message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • 55 mph on rural interstates
• 45 mph on urban interstates (unless posted otherwise)
• 35 mph on highways with 2–3 lanes (unless posted)
• 25 mph in school zones during school hours | Texas Transportation Code §§ 545.001‑545.004 | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts (except for certain motorcycle riders).
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Failure to buckle up can result in a $50 fine. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited (unless using a hands‑free system).
• Texting while driving is illegal. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal for drivers over 21.
• Lower BAC limits apply to commercial drivers and those under 21.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §§ 545.021, 545.022 | | **Reckless Driving** | • Driving with a willful disregard for safety.
• Penalties: up to 1 year in jail, fines up to $2,500, and license revocation. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at stop signs and red lights.
• Give right‑of‑way to emergency vehicles with flashing lights. | Texas Transportation Code §§ 545.021‑545.023 | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus stops to pick up or drop off children.
• Failure to stop can lead to a $200 fine. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or within 20 ft of a crosswalk.
• Parking in a handicap space without a valid permit is a $200 fine. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Most vehicles require an annual safety inspection. | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for total bodily injury, $25,000 for property damage. | Texas Insurance Code § 151.001 | | **Common Penalties** | • Fines range from $50 to $2,500 depending on offense.
• License points can lead to suspension after 12 points in 12 months.
• Jail time for serious offenses (e.g., DUI, reckless driving). | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | --- ### How to Stay Updated 1. **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – Official website: [dps.texas.gov](https://www.dps.texas.gov) *Provides current statutes, enforcement notices, and driver education resources.* 2. **Texas Transportation Code** – Accessible online via the Texas Legislature’s website: [statutes.capitol.texas.gov](https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov) *Full legal text of all traffic laws.* 3. **Texas DMV** – For registration, inspection, and insurance requirements: [dmv.texas.gov](https://www.dmv.org/tx/) 4. **Local County Courts** – For specific case law and recent rulings that may affect local traffic regulations. --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always check for posted speed limits**; they can change at construction sites or in school zones. - **Use hands‑free devices** if you need to make calls while driving. - **Keep your vehicle’s registration and inspection stickers up to date** to avoid fines. - **Carry proof of insurance** in your vehicle at all times. - **Be mindful of school buses**—stop and wait until the bus resumes motion. --- #### Need More Specific Information? If you’re looking for details on a particular type of violation (e.g., speeding, DUI), or you want to know how recent changes to the Texas Transportation Code might affect you, let me know! I can pull up the exact statutory language or point you toward relevant court cases.
